title: A clinical study evaluating DM199 in pregnant women undergoing expectant management for preterm preeclampsia
official: A Phase 1b/2a, Open-label Multi-Centre Dose-Escalation and Expansion Study of DM199, in Participants undergoing Expectant Management for Preterm Preeclampsia
summary:
Main objective: •To assess the safety and tolerability of DM199 in pregnant participants diagnosed with PE between 24⁰/₇ to 33⁰/₇ weeks gestation undergoing expectant management. 
•To measure the PK of DM199 in the fetal circulation via cord blood.
•To characterize the PK of DM199 in the maternal circulation.
•To measure PK of DM199 in breast milk or colostrum after birth.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Singleton pregnancy between 24⁰/₇ and 33⁰/₇ weeks GA (inclusive) with a viable fetus
2. 2. Age ≥ 18 years and able to give informed consent
3. 3. Diagnosis of PE or superimposed PE (significant proteinuria^a  must be present in both cases) • PE is defined, according to the International Society of Hyptertension in Pregnancy (ISSHP) (Magee et al, 2022), as the presence of de novo hypertension^b after 20 weeks’ gestation accompanied by proteinuria and/or  evidence of maternal acute kidney injury, liver dysfunction, neurological features, hemolysis or thrombocytopenia, and/or fetal growth restriction^c.  o Co-existing fetal growth restriction can be included as long as there is continuous forward flow in the umbilical artery.  • Superimposed PE is defined as loss of blood pressure control in a participant with pre-existing hypertension^d on medication, with either new onset proteinuria or more than a doubling of previous proteinuria levels for those who already have proteinuria.
4. 4. In persons with underlying chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages 1-3 without chronic hypertension, a diagnosis of PE as defined by the development of new onset hypertension with at least a doubling of baseline proteinuria
5. 5. Eligible for expectant management (beyond 48 hours)
6. 6. Body weight 50-130 kg (inclusive) at screening
7. 7. Participant consents to admission for inpatient expectant management of preterm PE until delivery
8. 8. Willing and able to comply with study procedures in the best judgement of the investigator.    a Significant proteinuria is defined as proteinuria ≥ 0.3 g/dL in a complete 24-hour urine collection; or a spot (random) urine sample with ≥30 mg/mmol urinary protein creatinine ratio.  b Hypertension in pregnancy is defined as systolic blood pressure ≥ 140 mmHg and/or a diastolic blood pressure ≥ 90 mmHg on the average of at least two measurements, taken at least 4 hours apart.  c Fetal growth restriction is defined as estimated fetal weight that is below the 10th percentile for gestational age, as measured by ultrasound.   d  Chronic (pre-existing) hypertension is defined as hypertension that pre-dates the pregnancy or appears before 20 weeks gestation.  e  Participants managed expectantly solely for purposes of completion of corticosteroid administration (and for planned birth as soon as the administration is complete) are not eligible.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Participants must not be enrolled into the study if they meet any of the exclusion criteria: 1. Severe end-organ complications of PE that mandate immediate delivery and preclude expectant management for current pregnancy: a) Eclampsia^a b) Pulmonary edema^b  c) Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets (HELLP)^c  syndrome  d) Severe renal involvement^d  e) Cerebrovascular event^e  f) Intractable headache unrelieved by analgesia g) Persistent visual disturbances h) Liver hematoma or rupture i) Refractory hypertension^f
2. 10. Known α₁-antitrypsin deficiency or known hereditary angioedema.
3. 11. Recent investigational exposure: currently participating in another interventional study or received an investigational drug/device within 90 days prior to screening or during the current pregnancy.
4. 12. Women with an active malignancy or history of any malignancy other than squamous or basal cell carcinoma of the skin.
5. 13. Substance use disorder (alcohol or drugs) with history/complications likely to affect safety or compliance.
6. 14. Unable or unwilling to comply with protocol requirements, including procedures, assessments and follow-up visits.
7. 15. Any condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, poses an undue risk or would interfere with the study conduct or interpretation.
8. 16. Absent or reversed flow in the umbilical artery.
9. 17. Suspicion or a diagnosis of a major fetal anomaly or malformation or chromosomal abnormality.  a Eclampsia defined as new onset of grand mal seizure activity and/or an unexplained coma during pregnancy with signs or symptoms of PE.  b Pulmonary edema defined as oxygen saturation less than 92% on room air with bibasal crepitations on auscultation and signs of pulmonary edema on chest X-ray.  c HELLP syndrome defined as a platelet count less than 100 × 10^9/L, aspartate aminotransferase greater than 70 IU/L, and hemolysis as demonstrated by lactate dehydrogenase > 600 IU/L or hemolysis on a peripheral blood smear.  d Severe renal involvement defined as creatinine level greater or equal to 97 µmol/L (1.1 mg/dL).  e Ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke associated with clinical symptoms and definitive signs on imaging.  f Refractory hypertension defined as need for continuous intravenous antihypertensive therapy.  g Placental abruption defined as separation of the placenta prior to birth of the fetus. Clinically it is diagnosed as a tense uterus with vaginal bleeding and confirmed after delivery with a retroplacental clot covering more than 15% of the maternal placental surface AND/OR placental pathology confirmation of basal plate disruption and a retroplacental haematoma.
10. 2. Placental abruption or a stillbirth.
11. 3. Fetal compromise that necessitates urgent delivery.
12. 4. Chronic Kidney Disease stage 4–5 (estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <30 mL/min/1.73m^2), or dialysis dependency.
13. 5. Uncontrolled thyroid disease despite medications.
14. 6. Underlying maternal cardiac disease that is clinically significant (e.g., significant arrhythmia, conduction abnormality, severe valvular disease, or congenital/acquired heart disease posing excess risk).
15. 7. Significant maternal vascular disease (e.g. renal artery stenosis).
16. 8. History of clinically significant allergic reactions (e.g., angioedema or anaphylaxis requiring hospitalization) or known allergy or hypersensitivity to DM199.
17. 9. Active infection requiring parenteral therapy or inpatient monitoring at enrollment (e.g., chorioamnionitis). Uncomplicated infections treated with oral antibiotics (e.g., urinary tract infection [UTI], sinusitis) are not exclusionary.
